statement: The trial command of gap gate-slow:test/budget.test.mjs ran twice in the tree on linux with v24.9.0 and took 3353 ms and 3435 ms of wall time (10 of 10 tests passing and 10 of 10 tests passing), against a bar of 15000 ms where the ledger measured 30574 ms on his PC, so barMet is true. The control, the same command on the file as committed at 8a55dc4, took 15229 ms and 15216 ms (9 of 10 passing and 9 of 10 passing), and a failing test stops at its failed assertion, so the control times are a lower bound for that file run whole. Run-to-run noise was 82 ms in the bar arm and 13 ms in the control arm; the gap between the arm means is 11829 ms. Nothing was held out: the same file on the same host was both tuned and timed, so the unseen host is his Windows PC at its next gate.
